landing.faqRefundsQ: What changed in how refunds are counted?
landing.faqRefundsA: A refund used to count as lost revenue, and stock recovered from a return was ignored. Now a refund lowers net sales, recovered cost comes off product cost, the payment fee is its own line, and a refund dated after the period end is shown as a separate adjustment.

unit.netRevenueFormula: Net revenue = revenue − refunds (revenue is gross sales after discount)
unit.cm1Formula: CM1 = (net revenue − net product cost) ÷ net revenue, where net product cost = product cost − recovered
unit.cm2Formula: CM2 = (net revenue − net product cost − shipping − payment fees − handling) ÷ net revenue; shipping includes return shipping
unit.cm3Formula: CM3 = (net revenue − net product cost − shipping − payment fees − handling − ads) ÷ net revenue; ads are allocated, not caused
unit.netFormula: Net margin = (operational contribution − fixed costs) ÷ net revenue
unit.fixedTip: Assumed: entered by you, kept in this browser, and saved with a decision.
unit.fixedHint: Rupees per period. Used only for the estimated net margin.
unit.correctedTip: Includes {{n}} orders with values you corrected on the import report.
unit.partialTip: Partial: {{n}} unknown orders are left out, never counted as zero.
unit.handlingTip: Handling includes {{inr}} per order, estimated for rows without handling_inr.
unit.title: Unit economics
unit.sub: Per period, over {{n}} computed orders. Percentages are of net revenue.
unit.subChannel: Ads are the channel spend, deducted once per channel.
unit.gateClosed: Unknown orders are left out, so these cover computed orders only; the headline margin stays hidden until refund facts are complete.
unit.disclaimer: Estimated operational, not statutory net profit.
unit.fixedSharedTip: Each row carries a share of the fixed costs in proportion to its net revenue (assumed).

definitions.title: How the ledger counts
definitions.netRevenueNote: Revenue is gross sales after discount; the same figure as net sales.
definitions.npc: net product cost = product cost − recovered product cost
definitions.npcNote: Stock that comes back from a return is subtracted once, never twice.
definitions.fee: Deducted separately, on its own line; never folded into shipping or product cost.
definitions.late: A refund dated after the period end is a prior-period adjustment: the period total stays as reported, and the restated total is shown next to it.

drawer.recoveryPending: Not yet recognised in this period: the refund is dated after the period end.
drawer.recoveryPartial: Recovery {{recovered}} of {{cost}}: {{lost}} of stock cost did not come back.
drawer.recoveryFull: All of the product cost came back to stock.
drawer.adsChannel: Ads move to the channel line in this mode; channel spend is {{note}}.

late.drawerNote: Refund dated {{date}} falls after the period end{{end}}. The period figure is never overwritten; the restated view sits beside it.
late.note: Refunds dated after the period end ({{end}}) stay out of the period total; the restated total shows them recognised.

attribution.tip: Attribution is allocation, not causation. Ads and channel spend are allocated, not caused: moving them between orders or channels never changes the total.

provenance.observedTip: Observed: comes from the imported orders.
